title: Random Number Generators
description: Random number generators turn entropy into values used for keys, nonces, and other security-sensitive operations. TRNGs obtain randomness from physical sources, while PRNGs and CSPRNGs expand an internal state and remain secure only when that state is seeded and managed correctly.

resources.title: NIST: Random Number Generation
resources.notes: Overview of entropy sources, random bit generation, PRNGs, and deterministic random bit generators.

resources.title: NIST Glossary: Pseudorandom Number Generator
resources.notes: Defines deterministic generators and the conditions under which a cryptographic PRNG can be unpredictable.

resources.title: Technical Deep Dive into the Entropy Issue
resources.notes: Shows how a hardware RNG integration error routed wallet seed generation through a software fallback PRNG.
